Chicken curry

Catering for my husbands men's group. These will be served with plain greek yoghurt and basmati rice. The curries were made the day before and the rice cooked in a 10 cup rice cooker at dinner time.
This looks so great! What's the recipe?

Ok sure recipes coming up :) They were very favourably received, only a bit of gravy left at the bottom of the chicken one and about 1 portion of the chickpea was left.

Chickpea Curry this is a dry curry

6 tins of chickpeas, drained and rinsed

140g tin of tomato paste

3 large onions, diced

1/2 a head of garlic, finely chopped

piece of fresh ginger about as big as two fingers together, peeled and grated

2 tablespoons of garam marsala

2 heaped teaspoons of Kasmiri chilli powder

water, butter, salt

2 tbsps butter into a large pot on a low/medium heat and add the onions. Fry the onions gently with a big pinch of salt until they are softened and starting to get a golden tinge, even a bit brown on the edges.

Add the ginger and garlic and fry a couple more minutes until fragrant.

Add the whole tin of tomato paste and fry for a few more minutes.

Add all spices and mix together then add the chickpeas and mix until they are coated with the tomatoey spicey onions.

Add enough water to make a small amount of gravy and cook for about 5 mins until its nearly dry again.

Take off the heat and leave for a few hours/a day to develop in flavour.

Chicken Curry this is a wet saucy curry

~2.4kg (~5.3lb) of boneless skinless chicken thighs

2 onions sliced into half moons

4L of chicken stock

3 - 4 tbspns Vadouvan Curry powder

2 heaped tbspns of plain flour

the other half of the head of garlic, roughly chopped

another 2 fingers worth of fresh ginger, finely diced

5 largish carrots

~300g of frozen peas

Chopped each chicken thigh up into 4 or 5 pieces and fried hard in vege oil until golden brown on the outside. This took about 5 or 6 pans of chicken to do cause you don't want to overcrowd the pan when you are frying or the chicken won't brown off. Take your time, its worth it, adds SO much flavour.

Add both the onions and fry off until softened then add the garlic and ginger and fry 4 or 5 mins.

Add the curry powder then the flour and fry for about 2 mins.

Add the stock and mix.

Put the browned chicken pieces and the carrot chunks in to the gravy and mix thoroughly.

Bring up to heat then cook on a low simmer for 45 mins to 1 hour until the gravy has reduced and thickened.

Add the frozen peas and simmer for a minute. (At this point I added the peas and turned off the heat because the curry was going to be reheated the next day.
